title: the connection hold resends a request an uninstrumented provider had already replayed
mechanism_summary: When a provider reports no replay count and its final wording is not recognised as a provider retry, the new hold treats an already-replayed failure as unreplayed and sends the identical body again, turning two primary requests into six.
missed_check: No Claude arm reviewed 6fc362cedd40, so no missed check applies.

finder_sections.text:
**1. P1 — The hold repeats requests already replayed by an uninstrumented provider.**  
`packages/coding-agent/src/session/turn-recovery.ts:1857–1884`

Reproduction: a local endpoint alternates:
- HTTP 503 with `Retry-After: 0`;
- an SSE error saying `upstream closed the connection`, without streamed content.

The real OpenAI completions provider has already sent two requests when it returns the error. However, `providerReplays` is undefined and the final wording is rejected by `isProviderRetryableError`. Recovery therefore repeats the whole pair twice.

| Source | Primary requests before fallback |
|---|---:|
| Pinned main-source control | **2** |
| Reviewed head | **6** |

**All six primary POST bodies have identical SHA-256 hashes.** A second reproduction—503 followed by reasoning and a genuinely truncated chunked response—produces **6 requests versus 4** in the control. The corresponding instrumented Anthropic path correctly reports one replay and falls back after two requests.

**Explicit replay verdict: yes, this head can resend a request that a lower layer already replayed.** This is counted endpoint evidence, not an inference about possible duplication.

real_because.quote: | Round-one probe | **4/4 pass**; delay defect remains closed |

title: a terminal HTTP status hidden deep in the cause chain leaves the new errno classification retryable
mechanism_summary: The finalizer strips Connection once it finds a deep 400/401 but keeps the newly added Transient bit, so a terminal status behind several Error causes is still treated as retryable.
missed_check: No Claude arm reviewed 6fc362cedd40, so no missed check applies.

finder_sections.text:
**2. P2 — Deep terminal HTTP statuses leave the new errno classification retryable.**  
`packages/ai/src/error/flags.ts:1030–1034,1108–1120`

Reproduction: put an errno on an outer Error with a generic message, then put HTTP 400 or 401 behind three intermediate Error causes. Tested all four new errno spellings.

- Deep 400: control `retriable=false`; head **`retriable=true`**, ID `135168`.
- Deep 401: control `retriable=false`; head **`retriable=true`**, ID `16912384`.

The finalizer removes Connection once it discovers the status, but retains the newly added Transient bit. Shallow versions correctly remain terminal.

A related persisted-message case also fails: `classifyMessage` given an existing `Connection | Transient` classification and text `HTTP 400 Bad Request` **retains Connection**, because its finalizer does not receive the status parsed from the text.

`packages/ai/src/error/flags.ts:682–715`


title: a caller-supplied client or fetch reports providerReplays 0 instead of unknown, and the hold multiplies the request
mechanism_summary: The counting guard only excludes the private transport argument, so a public `options.client` or a self-retrying supplied fetch returns the untouched counter as zero, and the recovery then holds and resends a request the caller's own transport already replayed.
missed_check: No Claude arm reviewed f36efc41209a, so no missed check applies.

finder_sections.text:
### 1. P2 — Caller-owned clients still produce a false zero and multiply retries

**Files:** [`anthropic.ts:1823,2017–2018,3655`](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/f36efc41209a6a0b1fcc80ad31489b0ade9e2924/packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts#L1823), `wire-attempts.ts:42–46`.

The guard excludes the private `transport` argument, **not public `options.client`**. `resolveClient()` returns that supplied client before installing the counting fetch, but failure handling still reports the untouched counter as `0`.

A real caller-owned `AnthropicMessagesClient` sent a 503 request, retried, streamed thinking, and failed:

```text
caller-client: requests=2, providerReplays=0
```

Through `AgentSession`, this becomes the original multiplication defect:

```text
requests=6
models=[anthropic, anthropic, anthropic, openai]
counts=[0, 0, 0]
```

Expected: two primary requests, then fallback.

A supplied **fetch that retries internally** has the same blind spot:

```text
custom-fetch-retry: actual requests=2, fetch invocations=1, providerReplays=0
```

Returning `undefined` alone is not a complete remedy for opaque transports: the recovery probe also confirms that **unknown provenance plus streamed content takes the hold**. The producer and consumer must agree on what is actually known.

real_because.quote: Unchanged caller-fetch probes now report unknown, not zero.

title: the Vertex OAuth token request rides the request counter and is reported as a model replay
mechanism_summary: `createVertexAuthenticatedFetch` resolves the access token through the same `baseFetch` the wire counter wraps, so the metadata token request increments `WireAttempts.count` and a later wire cut on that call reports `providerReplays: 1`, silently disabling the hold on the Vertex Anthropic route.
missed_check: Searched the astra round-5 report for 'vertex', 'token', 'OAuth', 'getVertexAccessToken' and 'metadata.google': no hit. Its nearest counter text is the additional-attacks list, 'Native 307 redirect: two POSTs per call, reports zero. This remains the documented distinction between redirect hops and repository-owned replay attempts', and its file-by-file line '`stream.ts`: missing aggregation across authentication retries' — the authentication wrapper, not the Vertex token fetch.

finder_sections.text:
### 1. The Vertex OAuth token request is counted as a model request attempt (low–medium, measured)

`createVertexAuthenticatedFetch` (`packages/ai/src/stream.ts:721-747`) resolves the access token through the same `baseFetch` the counter rides on: `getVertexAccessToken({ signal, fetch: baseFetch })` at line 724. The token request therefore increments `WireAttempts.count` exactly like a model request.

Reproduction: a `google-vertex` / `anthropic-messages` model on a `:streamRawPredict` base URL, `globalThis.fetch` replaced, the metadata token endpoint answering a token and the model endpoint answering one complete SSE turn, driven through `stream()`.

```
urls: [ "http://metadata.google.internal/computeMetadata/v1/instance/service-accounts/default/token",
        "https://…/publishers/anthropic/models/claude-sonnet-4-5:streamRawPredict" ]
stopReason: stop providerReplays: 1
```

One model request went out; the message reports one replay. `getVertexAccessToken` caches in module scope (`google-auth.ts:290-331`), so this hits the first call of a process and every hourly refresh. Consequence: on that call a statusless wire cut reports `providerReplays: 1`, `#holdsChainForConnectionRetry` returns false, and the Vertex Anthropic route silently keeps the old immediate-fallback behaviour. The direction is safe — it suppresses holds, never invents one — but it contradicts what `AssistantMessage.providerReplays` (`types.ts:1339-1376`) and `wire-attempts.ts:3-34` say the number is. One-line fix: hand `getVertexAccessToken` the fetch from *below* the counter rather than `baseFetch`.

Control: the same probe against a non-rawPredict URL (no Vertex wrapper) reported `providerReplays: 10` for the 11 requests the Anthropic client's own loop made — the counter is right when the token path is not in play.

real_because.quote: | Vertex OAuth request overcount | **Closed, provenance limitation** | Native TLS test: cold, cached, and refreshed token paths made 2 token requests and 3 model requests; replay reports `[0,0,0]`. |

Its nearest text is 'Apart from finding 1, I found no path where a request leaves and the count does not rise.'

finder_sections.text:
### 1. P1 — Authentication retries still report zero after two requests

Locations:
- `packages/ai/src/stream.ts:1253–1284,1347–1369`
- `packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts:1838–1847`

`streamSimpleRequest()` retries with another resolved key. Each inner Anthropic call snapshots a new `wireStart`; the authentication wrapper forwards the last call’s report without including earlier attempts.

Native-fetch reproduction, **without a supplied fetch or client**:

1. First request receives HTTP 401.
2. The repository’s authentication loop resolves another key.
3. The replacement request streams thinking and fails with `read ECONNRESET`.
4. The returned message reports **`providerReplays: 0`**.

Both requests have the same SHA-256 body hash.

| Full-session measurement | Merged main control | This head |
|---|---:|---:|
| Primary requests before successful fallback | 2 | **6** |
| Reports from failed primary calls | absent | **0, 0, 0** |

All six primary bodies on head are identical. The counter sees the requests, but its reporting boundary discards earlier authentication attempts. Moving the counter below fetch wrappers did not finish the accounting contract.

Evidence: `auth-replay-fixed-head` and `auth-replay-fixed-main`, both exit **0**.

real_because.quote: | Authentication retry undercount | **Closed** | Direct call: 2 requests, reported replay count 1. Full session: 2 primary requests plus successful fallback, not 6 primary requests. Each primary pair has one body hash. |

title: `abortRetry()` called at the replay-report event clears the hold state and lets the same recovery hold a second model
mechanism_summary: The public `abortRetry()` clears both hold fields instead of ending the recovery, so a cancellation that lands while the held call reports its replays lets the still-running recovery hold again after its model-budget reset — 25 requests before the fallback succeeds.
missed_check: Searched the Claude round-5 report for 'abortRetry', 'cancel', 'reset' and 'race': the report has no cancellation probe at all. Its nearest hold-state text is finding 3, 'A hold can be charged without being taken (low, code read)', which is about `#connectionHoldsSpent` being incremented outside its consumer, not about a public cancellation reopening the hold.

finder_sections.text:
### 2. P2 — A public retry reset racing a replay report reopens the hold

Locations:
- `packages/coding-agent/src/session/turn-recovery.ts:909–912,2757–2764,3379–3382`
- Public entry: `AgentSession.abortRetry()`; also exposed by RPC `abort_retry`.

I called `session.abortRetry()` when the held Sonnet call emitted its terminal message reporting ten replays. This clears both hold fields. The pending recovery then continues; its later model-budget reset permits Haiku to hold again.

Observed sequence:

- Sonnet: **12 requests**, reports **0 then 10**
- Opus: **1 request**, reports **0**
- Haiku: **12 requests**, reports **0 then 10**
- OpenAI: **1 successful request**

That is **25 requests before successful fallback**, with two held calls spending provider budgets. No new prompt was submitted. Each model’s repeated request bodies had one SHA-256 hash.

This is a controlled cancellation race, not a claim about its production frequency. The public cancellation must stop the old recovery, or its state must survive while that recovery can still continue.

Evidence: `life-reset-race`, exit **0**.

real_because.quote: | `abortRetry()` reopened the hold at replay-report time | **Closed for that reproduction** | Counts now **12/1/1/1**: 14 requests before success, 15 total. No second held provider budget. |

title: the held-sleep bound compares with `<=`, so a hint exactly equal to the window is still taken and the promised strict bound is reached
mechanism_summary: The hint comparison is inclusive while the documented window and the acceptance criteria are strict, so hints that sum to exactly 1,500 ms or 16,000 ms are accepted and the scheduled held sleep equals, instead of staying under, the promised bound.
missed_check: Searched the Claude round-5 report for '<=', 'inclusive', 'strict', 'equal' and 'boundary': none. Its bound section measures only interior values and concludes they are inside the window — 'Added sleep at the 500 ms default base: observed held delays **40.5 ms** and **921.1 ms**, sum **961.6 ms** — inside the claimed 1.5 s, and each inside its own `[0, min(500·2^(k-1), 8 s))` window.' It never drives the exact-boundary hint.

finder_sections.text:
### 4. P2 — Equality still violates the promised strict sleep bounds

Location: `packages/coding-agent/src/session/turn-recovery.ts:3041–3044`.

The comparison is `<=`, although the documented windows and acceptance criteria are strict.

Real-timer measurements:

| Case | Scheduled held sleep | First request to fallback |
|---|---:|---:|
| Default base; hints `try again in 500ms`, then `1000ms` | **1,500 ms** | **1.613 s** |
| 8,000 ms base; two 8,000 ms hints | **16,000 ms** | **16.061 s** |

These are no longer the former 18-second overrun, but neither is **under** its promised bound. The duration wording avoids the separate numeric-metadata defect above.

Other bound attacks:
- Growing hints 400 → 900 → 1,800 ms: **1,300 ms** held sleep; then fallback.
- Second hint 1,001 ms: only the first **400 ms** hold occurs.
- Two hints in one error: the parser selected the first; no bound extension occurred.
- Mutating the failed message during its wait did not extend the current timer; the next 9,000 ms hint caused fallback. This last probe is a state-mutation attack, not a real post-terminal provider event.

real_because.quote: | Inclusive sleep bound | **Closed** | Exact 500-ms/default and 8000-ms/maximum hints now decline the hold: one primary request, then fallback, **0 ms held sleep**. |

Location: `packages/ai/src/error/flags.ts:514–540,658–684`.

The URL/header-name repair works, but numeric metadata **values** still become status or capacity evidence:

| Diagnostic suffix after `read ECONNRESET` | Connection | Retriable |
|---|---:|---:|
| `retry-after-ms=400` | true | true |
| `retry-after-ms=401` | false | **false** |
| `retry-after-ms=403` | false | **false** |
| `retry-after-ms=429` | false | true |
| `retry-after-ms=500` | false | true |
| `retry-after-ms=503` | false | true |
| `retry-after-ms=529` | false | **false** |

`elapsed_ms=` produces the same results. These are durations, not rejected credentials or HTTP statuses.

The real-provider `retry-after-ms=503` endpoint case reports zero but falls back after **one primary request**, with no hold. This is another uncovered input in the metadata-classification defect class, not a claim that every listed behavior was newly introduced by this head.

Evidence: `classifier-extra` and `bound-attacks-head`, exit **0**.

finder_sections.text:
### Open finding — P2

[`packages/ai/src/utils/retry-after.ts:25–36`](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/08773d3241a9290374aa3b150dd57ab158c866c2/packages/ai/src/utils/retry-after.ts#L25-L36) discards a longer response-header hint when the error already contains `retry-after-ms=`.

Fresh evidence:

- Body hint **200 ms**, header `Retry-After: 9`: the shared reader receives only **200 ms**.
- Through real `coworkFetch` TLS, a oneshot schedules **200 ms** and resends the identical body after **253 ms**, instead of declining the 9000-ms wait under its 1000-ms cap. **Zero runtime fetch calls.**
- The actual credential-rotation consumer persists a **200-ms block**. Longer-body and header-only controls correctly persist **9000 ms**.

`hint-reader`, `hint-wire`, and corrected `hint-auth` each exit **1**. This formatter defect **predates the reader move**; it is not a new regression or a failure of the repeated-text fix. The longer header must survive formatting.

real_because.quote:
- **Done, pushed, verified.** GPT P2: a shorter body hint hid a longer header wait. `formatErrorMessageWithRetryAfter`
  appends the header wait as the final token unless the message's own reading is at least as long.

mechanism_summary: The reader cannot tell the formatter's appended final token from provider text, so a body or SSE error event whose last token is `retry-after-ms=86400000` overrides the real `Retry-After: 0.2` header and persists an 86,400,000 ms credential block — up to `Number.MAX_VALUE`, confirmed still stored by an independent SQLite read.

finder_sections.text:
1. **P1 — Open: the declared final-token residual can persist an effectively permanent credential block.**  
   [`retry-after.ts:14–49`](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/21106b0d3842a9069c1ecd9fad3325f9ccf5b2bb/packages/ai/src/utils/retry-after.ts#L14) cannot distinguish a formatter token from provider text.

   **Residual verdict: unacceptable.** Header timing needs identifiable provenance, not an indistinguishable body suffix.

**P3 — the residual bites the producer the lane itself called plausible.** `retry-after-ms=200; quoted upstream response: retry-after-ms=9000` → head 9,000, main 200 (45×): r9's "gateway quotes the upstream body underneath", with the quote last. The echo inside JSON no longer bites — `…{"prompt":"retry-after-ms=86400000"}` reads **200**, block **201 ms** (was 86,400,001).

- Streamed errors with the same `Retry-After: 9` and a 200-ms body hint: field **absent**, credential block **200 ms**, one-shot callback retried after **200 ms**.

### Open finding — P2
